Rashi on Gittin 37b:10:1.hebrew: אי לפני יאוש - של בעלים הראשונים, פדאוהו מן העובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:10:1.english: If [it was] before despairing - of the first owners, [that] they redeemed him from the idolater:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:10:2.hebrew: לשום עבד אמאי ישתעבד - וקס"ד לרבו ראשון, ואמאי? הרי נתייאש:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:10:2.english: To be a slave, why will he be a slave - And [the Gemara] assumes [this refers] to his first master; and why [should he be enslaved to him]? Behold, he [has already] despaired [of recovering him]:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:11:1.hebrew: ולשום עבד - על מנת להחזירו לרבו ראשון, או אפי' על מנת להשתעבד בו:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:11:1.english: And to be a slave - [meaning, he redeemed him] on condition to return him to his first master, or even on condition to enslave him [himself]:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:11:2.hebrew: ישתעבד לרבו ראשון - דשני לא קנה, דמידע ידע דלא פקע שם מריה מיניה לפני יאוש, והרי הוא כגוזלו ממנו:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:11:2.english: He will be a slave to his first master - Because the second [master] has not acquired [him], for he surely knows that his [first] master's ownership has not departed from him before despairing [of recovering him], and he is like one who steals him from him:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:12:1.english: So [too], it is a mitzvah to redeem slaves - and there is no [reason] to be concerned that [people] will refrain and not redeem [them]:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:13:1.english: To his second master - And later [the Gemara] asks: From whom did he acquire him?

Rashi on Gittin 37b:14:1.hebrew: בין כך ובין כך ישתעבד - לרבו ראשון, כדחזקיה:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:14:1.english: Both in this [case] and in that [case] he will be a slave - to his first master, in accordance with [the statement of] Chizkiyah:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:15:1.hebrew: בשלמא לאביי - דמוקי בלפני יאוש, וטעמא דת"ק משום מימנעי ולא פרקי:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:15:1.english: Granted, according to Abaye - who establishes [the Mishnah as referring to a case] before [the owner's] despairing, and the reason of the first Tanna [is] because [otherwise people] would refrain and not redeem [slaves]:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:15:2.hebrew: היינו דקאמר כשם - דאיהו לא חייש למימנעי ולא פרקי, משום דמצוה לפדותו:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:15:2.english: This is [the reason] that he said, "Just as" - For he [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] is not concerned that [people] will refrain and not redeem [slaves], because it is a mitzvah to redeem him:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:16:1.hebrew: אלא לרבא - דמוקי בלאחר יאוש, וטעמא דת"ק משום אפקעתא דיאוש הוא — מאי "כשם" דקאמר? הא טעמא דרשב"ג משום דחזקיה, שלא יפיל עצמו לגייסות, הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:16:1.english: However, according to Rava - who establishes [the Mishnah as referring to] after despairing [by the owner], and the reason of the Tanna Kamma is because of the release [effected by] despairing — what is [the meaning of] "just as" that he says? Behold, the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is because of [the statement] of Chizkiyah, so that [a slave] will not throw himself [into the hands of] marauding troops:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:19:1.hebrew: למעשה ידיו - וישראל קני ליה מידו למעשה ידיו בכספא, ולגופיה בטבילה לשם עבדות, כדאמרינן ביבמות בהחולץ (יבמות דף מז:). ואפילו מל וטבל גבי רבו ראשון, קנייה שבאי ביאוש למעשה ידיו, דהא אפי' ישראל נמי מיקני ליה לעובד כוכבים למעשה ידיו; ונהי דישראל נפיק מיניה ביובל, אבל עבד משתעבד לעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:19:1.english: With regard to his labor - And a Jew acquires him from his [the captor's] hand with regard to his labor through money, and [acquires] his person through immersion for the sake of slavery, as we say in [Tractate] Yevamot, in [the chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 47b). And even if he [the slave] had been circumcised and immersed [while] with his first master, the captor acquires him through [the first master's] despair [of recovering him] with regard to his labor; for even a Jew is also acquired by an idolater with regard to his labor — and although a Jew goes free from him in the Jubilee [year], a [Canaanite] slave, however, remains enslaved forever:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:19:2.hebrew: מהם תקנו - רבוי' הוא, דהא כתיב לעיל מיניה "מהם תקנו עבד ואמה", וכתיב בתרי' "וגם מבני התושבים הגרים עמכם", ולישתוק:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:19:2.english: Of them you may acquire - This is an amplification [i.e., a superfluous repetition], for it is written above it: "Of them you may acquire a male slave and a female slave" [Leviticus 25:44], and it is written after it: "Moreover, of the children of the strangers who sojourn among you" — and it should have remained silent [without repeating "of them you may acquire"]:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:1:1.hebrew: המחזיר חוב לחבירו בשביעית - בזמן שהשביעית נוהגת, ועברה עליו שביעית ואח"כ החזירו; ולא שהחזירו בשביעית עצמה, דא"כ לא הוה צריך למימר "משמט אני", דקי"ל: אין שביעית משמטת אלא בסופה:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:1:1.english: One who repays a debt to his friend during the Sabbatical [Year] - [That is,] at a time when the Sabbatical [Year] is in force, and the Sabbatical [Year] passed over it [the debt] and afterwards he repaid it; and not that he repaid it during the Sabbatical [Year] itself, for if so, he would not need to say "I abrogate [the debt]," as we hold [as established law] that the Sabbatical [Year] only abrogates [debts] at its end:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:1:2.english: [He] must - [i.e.,] the lender [must] say to him: "I abrogate [the debt]."

Rashi on Gittin 37b:1:3.hebrew: ואם אמר לו אע"פ כן - "אני רוצה להחזירו לך":
Rashi on Gittin 37b:1:3.english: And if he said to him, "Even so" - [meaning,] "I want to return it to you":

Rashi on Gittin 37b:1:4.english: As it is stated: “And this is the manner [devar] of the abrogation” - [He] must utter a statement [dibbur] of abrogation:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:2:1.hebrew: ותלי ליה - אם היה רוצה לחזור בו, יתלנו על עץ אם גברה ידו, עד דאמר ליה "אע"פ כן":
Rashi on Gittin 37b:2:1.english: And he hangs him - if [the debtor] wanted to retract, [the creditor] may hang him on a tree if he has the upper hand, until he says to him, "Even so":

Rashi on Gittin 37b:2:2.hebrew: עד דאמר הכי - "במתנה אני נותן לך", ואין כאן משום "לא יגוש", דלא בבי דינא קתבע ליה ולאו משום חוב:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:2:2.english: Until he says this - "I am giving [it] to you as a gift," and there is no [prohibition] here of "he shall not exact [it]," because he is not claiming it from him in court, and [it is] not on account of a debt:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:3:1.hebrew: הוה מסיק ביה רבה זוזי - היה נושה בו מעות, רבה היה המלוה:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:3:1.english: Rabbah was claiming zuzim from him - He was a creditor to him for money; Rabbah was the lender:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:4:1.english: He went to him - Abaye came to Abba bar Marta:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:4:2.hebrew: אמר - רבה: לא הוה ביה דעתא בהאי מדרבנן מעיקרא, דהוה ליה למימר "אע"פ כן":
Rashi on Gittin 37b:4:2.english: He said - [This refers to] Rabba [who said]: "This scholar did not have the sense at first," [for] he should have said, "Nevertheless":

Rashi on Gittin 37b:5:1.english: Since the Sages instituted the prosbol - and [thus] he is able to collect [his debt] in a permitted manner:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:5:2.hebrew: לא שביק היתירא - דמלוה בלא פרוזבול, למימר "הוה לי ואבד", ואכיל איסורא:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:5:2.english: He does not leave aside the permitted - [such] that he would lend without a prosbol, to say "I had [one] and it was lost," and eat what is forbidden:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:7:1.hebrew: הרי אלו לא יפרעו - בכתובות בפרק הכותב; אלמא לא מהימן לומר "היה לי ואבד", דעל כרחיך בדטעין "היה לי ואבד" עסקינן, דאי לאו הכי — צריכא למימר דשביעית משמטת:
Rashi on Gittin 37b:7:1.english: These may not be collected - [This Mishnah is] in Ketubot, in the chapter [entitled] HaKotev; thus, he is not believed to say, "I had [a prosbol] and it was lost," for perforce we are dealing with [a case] where he claims, "I had [one] and it was lost," since if not so, would it need to be stated that the Sabbatical year cancels [the debt]?

Rashi on Gittin 37b:8:1.english: He does not need [to] - for he is believed to say [that it] was lost:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:9:2.english: That was captured and they redeemed him - [i.e.,] other Jews [redeemed him]:

Rashi on Gittin 37b:9:3.english: He will be a slave - In the Gemara, [it] explains [this]:

Tosafot on Gittin 37b:11:1.hebrew: לעולם לפני יאוש כו' - "לרבו שני לא, דהא לשום בן חורין פרקיה"; ה"ה דמצי למימר: "לרבו שני לא, דהא לפני יאוש הוא":
Tosafot on Gittin 37b:11:1.english: Actually, [it is] before despairing, etc. - "[He will] not [be a slave] to his second master, because he redeemed him as a freeman"; similarly, [Abaye] could have said: "[He will] not [be a slave] to his second master, because it is before [the owner's] despairing":

Tosafot on Gittin 37b:11:2.hebrew: דלמא מימנעי ולא פרקי ליה - וא"ת: מהאי טעמא, כשפדאו לשום עבד, ישתעבד לרבו שני? וי"ל: דמטעם זה אין ראוי לגזול לזה את עבדו וליתנו לחבירו, ולא שייך האי טעמא אלא כשפודהו לשם מצוה, לשם בן חורין:
Tosafot on Gittin 37b:11:2.english: Lest they refrain and not redeem him - And if you say: For this reason, when he redeemed him to be a slave, he should be enslaved to his second master? One can answer: For this reason it is not proper to rob this one of his slave and give him to his fellow; and this reason only applies when he redeems him for the sake of a mitzvah, to be a freeman:

Tosafot on Gittin 37b:14:1.hebrew: בין כך ובין כך ישתעבד כדחזקיה - פירש בקונטרס: לרבו ראשון. וכן מגיה ר"ת; דאי כשפדאו לשם עבד ישתעבד לשני, יפיל עצמו לגייסו' כדי שירויח לענין מציאה ומתנה, דלא קני ליה שני אלא למעשה ידיו; ופעמים נמי שהוא שונא לרבו ראשון מתמול שלשום ומפקיע עצמו ממנו. ומיהו נוכל לומר דלא פליג ר' שמעון בן גמליאל אתנא קמא אלא בפדאו לשום בן חורין, דמשום דבר מועט לא יפיל עצמו לגייסות:
Tosafot on Gittin 37b:14:1.english: Both in this [case] and in that [case] he will be a slave, in accordance with [the statement] of Ḥizkiyya - Rashi explained: to his first master. And so does Rabbeinu Tam emend [the text]; for if, when [the second person] redeemed him as a slave, he were to be enslaved to the second [master], he would hand himself over to [gentile] troops in order to profit with respect to a found object and a gift, since the second [master] acquires him only for his handiwork; and sometimes too, he hates his first master from before, and [thus] releases himself from him. However, we can say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees with the first Tanna only where he redeemed him as a free man, for on account of a small matter he would not hand himself over to troops:

Tosafot on Gittin 37b:17:1.hebrew: אי לפני יאוש קאמריתו - אע"פ שמסתפק ר' שמעון בן גמליאל בדברי רבנן, מ"מ לא מסתבר ליה לרבא כלל לומר דפליג לפני יאוש:
Tosafot on Gittin 37b:17:1.english: If you are speaking of before despairing - Even though Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is uncertain about the Rabbis' words, nevertheless, it does not seem reasonable to Rava at all to say that he disagrees before despairing:

Tosafot on Gittin 37b:4:1.hebrew: לא שביק היתירא ואכיל איסורא - אומר ר"ת דמהאי טעמא נאמן אפי' בלא שבועה:
Tosafot on Gittin 37b:4:1.english: One does not leave aside what is permitted and eat what is forbidden - Rabbeinu Tam says that for this reason [the lender] is believed even without an oath:
